final.answer: Along the path from BV-1-1 to P-12-2, the items with datasheets are BV-1-1 and P-2-1 (P-12-2 has no datasheet in the description). The lowest maximum allowable pressure belongs to P-2-1, the Gorman-Rupp pump, whose datasheet gives a maximum operating pressure of 250 psi (1723 kPa) at up to 100 F (37°C), with a footnote to consult the factory for applications exceeding this. The BV-1-1 datasheet (Flowserve Worcester F51/F52) contains no maximum allowable pressure value in the retrieved data — only stem torque values and seat-material temperature ratings — so no pressure rating can be given for it.

final.answer: Two items receive flow directly from E-14-1: the centrifugal pump P-14-2 and the ball valve TV-14-1. Per its datasheet, P-14-2 has a maximum allowable operating pressure of 250 psi (1723 kPa) up to 100 °F (37 °C), based on system component limitations (maximum casing pressure 266 psi / 1834 kPa). TV-14-1 has no single maximum pressure: its datasheet gives a pressure/temperature rating chart, so the limit depends on the valve's pressure class, body material group and seat material — for example about 19.8 bar (Group 1.2, Class 150) or 51.8 bar (Group 1.2, Class 300) when cold, and seat materials like PTFE dropping to 0 bar near their temperature limits. Since the datasheet extract does not state which class, material or operating temperature applies to this valve, its exact rating cannot be pinned down from the description alone. Of the firm values available, the pump's 250 psi (about 17 bar) is the lowest clearly stated limit, being below the valve's listed body ratings at comparable moderate temperatures; however, at elevated temperatures a soft-seated valve rating could fall below the pump's limit, so a definitive 'lowest' for TV-14-1 cannot be confirmed from the information given.

final.answer: Two items receive flow directly from E-14-1: pump P-14-2 and valve TV-14-1. Per its datasheet, P-14-2 has a maximum operating pressure rating at temperatures up to 100 F (37 °C), and its seal detail limits the maximum temperature of liquid pumped to 160 °F (71 °C). TV-14-1's datasheet gives pressure/temperature ratings per ASME B16.34 with maximum seat temperature ratings that depend on the seat material (e.g., 600 °F/315 °C for metal or PEEK, 500 °F/260 °C for Fluorofill, 450 °F/230 °C for reinforced or virgin PTFE, 200 °F/90 °C for UHMWPE, 180 °F/80 °C for Delrin); the description does not state which seat material is actually fitted, so a single maximum fluid temperature for TV-14-1 cannot be given. Of the stated values, P-14-2 has the lowest limit, 100 F (37 °C) for its maximum operating pressure.
